newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Accused plutonium smuggler returned to Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Accused plutonium smuggler returned to Colombia.

text.p: A Colombian man who grabbed world headlines when he was caught smuggling plutonium between Russia and Germany in 1994 returned home on Thursday after serving nearly three years in prison in Germany.
"I'm very content, very happy and excited," Justiniano Torres, a physician, told reporters at Bogota El Dorado international airport.

Justiniano, who was deported aboard a Lufthansa flight from Germany, was unable to elaborate as police agents bustled him into an armour-plated car for what one official described as a "debriefing" at state security police headquarters.
Police sources said no charges were pending against Justiniano in Colombia, however, and he was expected to be released soon.

Justiniano served nearly three years in a German prison after his arrest on charges he belonged to an international arms ring. He was convicted after being caught in the act of smuggling just more than a pound (0.5 kg) of plutonium aboard a flight from the former Soviet Union to Germany.
